dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The two May dealer files accepted every received row and reconciled cash to ledger with zero difference and zero duplicate-source-event flags."
"The 31-May cluster contains 17 annual renewals: DLR-104 has 8 rows/$723.42 and DLR-219 has 9 rows/$782.87."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "My inference is that the cluster reflects scheduled dealer-batch timing."
"The operations email describes monthly annual-renewal files using the dealer transaction date as effective date and month-end as posting date."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "That inference is strong for duplication and pipeline-integrity questions but does not settle accounting recognition or subscriber fulfilment."
"Subscriber entitlement activation status" and "Governing revenue-recognition reporting clock" are listed as material unknowns with decision-changing evidence.

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The single immediate next action is executing a read-only audit query" evaluating entitlement provisioning status.
"Keep restatement on hold pending the verification outcome."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision: Do not escalate. No revenue restatement, billing reversal, or pipeline remediation is warranted."
"Failed activations would change the decision to escalate a provisioning defect; successful activation would support closing that unknown."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Cross-checking the raw files against operational claims confirms that the 17-row 31-May cluster is an expected month-end batch ... on contractually permitted terms" — the cited files support the timing pattern and reconciliation, but contractually permitted terms are not specifically evidenced.

"Reconciling dealer settlement cycles against bank remittance logs confirms that funds arrived in accordance with monthly credit agreements without revenue inflation" — no bank remittance log source, query, or supporting detail is provided in the submission or cited evidence table.

"Revenue Manipulation: rejected" and "no evidence of billing manipulation" are somewhat stronger than the available checks support; the evidence supports no duplicate-source events, complete acceptance, and cash reconciliation, but does not independently prove absence of all manipulation.
"No ... pipeline remediation is warranted" is broader than the evidence because downstream event-time analytics may still require remediation or documented use of effective_event_date.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the main alternatives of a pipeline defect, revenue manipulation, entitlement failure, and accounting-clock mismatch. The strongest missed or underdeveloped alternative is that the pattern is financially benign but still creates a downstream analytics/reporting defect if consumers use posted_at rather than effective_event_date; the submission raises reporting-clock uncertainty but does not explicitly recommend effective_event_date for event-time analytics.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a reproducible join/query showing the 90 West rows mapped to the two import files with unique source_event_ids, cash totals, and entitlement outcomes, and explicitly require downstream event-time analyses to use effective_event_date while treating the email and any bank-remittance claim only as corroboration.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South NO_SIGNAL tickets fell from 51 in May to 28 in June, but service-event data still records 10 May events affecting 9,409 accounts and 8 June events affecting 7,045 accounts."
"Containment rate is 64.8% if pre-auth sessions are excluded versus 56.1% if all interactions count in the denominator."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Apparent complaint reduction is heavily driven by 650 pre-authentication drops and automated ticket-creation suppression rather than verified self-service resolution."
"The recording process changed, so the case-count denominator changed with it."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "I cannot test whether failed-authentication customers contact SkyWave again without a read-only subscriber-level 7-day callback/recontact query."
"A high repeat rate keeps rollout on hold; a low rate makes genuine containment more credible."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Decision: Defer national expansion and maintain existing South pilot boundaries."
"Keep the rollout decision on hold pending the result."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The single next action is one targeted, read-only 7-day repeat-contact/callback query reconciled to all NOVA sessions."
"What formal written criteria, benchmark thresholds, and observation windows govern the decision to proceed with national expansion?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "New self-service stages balance_check (29.1% of sessions) and pack_info (21.3%) ... representing genuine deflection for authenticated callers." Stage completion alone does not establish successful resolution or improved experience.

"The 650 pre-authentication drops ... represent uncaptured customer friction rather than successful self-service resolution." Abandonment and failed authentication indicate possible lost measurement, but do not by themselves prove complaint or dissatisfaction.

"Analysis ... confirms that the apparent drop is an artifact of measurement changes." The evidence strongly supports a measurement-change hypothesis, but does not establish that it explains all of the reduction without journey linkage, repeat-contact analysis, or call review.

"these sessions have no verified customer case in the CareDesk view." Absence from the viewed case data supports missing observable case creation, not necessarily absence of downstream recovery or contact.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled the benign alternative that failed-authentication customers may have recovered without contacting SkyWave: it explicitly preserves that possibility and proposes repeat-contact evidence, stating that a low repeat rate would make genuine containment more credible. It missed or underdeveloped the possibility that authenticated balance or pack-information sessions genuinely resolved customer needs while the apparent ticket reduction was partly measurement-driven and partly real.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add end-to-end journey validation before treating the result as either failure or success: link NOVA sessions to subsequent contacts and outcomes, stratified by terminal stage and authentication result, and review a sampled set of calls. A repeat-contact query is valuable but a low repeat rate alone would not prove satisfaction or resolution.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv`, rows 1–4 and specific fields for severity, duration, impact, clearance, timestamps, and inverter IDs.
It explicitly distinguishes the extract's observations from its limitation: “constant fields cannot distinguish affected from healthy units.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It cross-checks severity labels against `impact_mw=0`, `cleared=yes`, duration, dates, and inverter distribution rather than treating `COMM_LINK_WARN` as proof of equipment failure.
It identifies export completeness as the key alternative explanation, but does not independently test the communications-warning mechanism against telemetry or communications logs.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It states that the export has only four rows, lacks a plant-wide denominator and extraction filter, and that constant fields cannot distinguish affected from healthy units.
It conditions closure on an unfiltered query: “If additional open faults or nonzero-impact events appear, re-evaluate.”

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation—“Hold escalation and execute one cheap completeness check”—is proportionate to cleared, zero-impact observations.
The proposed read-only export query is a discriminating next test and preserves operational constraints without inventing a plant problem.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately scopes the finding to the supplied file: “The four observed events represent isolated, self-resolving occurrences totalling 13 minutes with zero generation loss in `inverter_events.csv`.”
It appropriately treats the mixed wording and seven-minute warning as a reason for a low-priority scope check, not operational escalation.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Low-severity” and “isolated” are reasonable summaries but are somewhat stronger than the CSV alone proves, particularly because the export denominator and completeness are unknown.
“This query is completely safe and reversible” is plausible for a read-only query but is not independently established by the supplied evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The seven-minute `COMM_LINK_WARN` could reflect a recurring communications reliability issue even with zero recorded MW impact and cleared status. The current extract does not establish recurrence, so this supports a conditional quality check rather than escalation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State the exact completeness check and, if it confirms the four-row scope, optionally cross-check the seven-minute warning against communications or inverter telemetry to distinguish a benign transient from a recurring communications-quality issue.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites specific fields from dispatch_blocks.csv, including base_schedule_mw, submitted_schedule_mw, actual_mw, dsm_rate_rs_kwh, and schedule_source.
It explicitly reproduces the cross-day calculation: '(662,444.09 - 453,085.88) / 662,444.09 = 31.6%'.
It distinguishes observed arithmetic from causal interpretation, labeling arithmetic confidence high and causal interpretation medium.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission identifies that the 31.6% comparison uses different dates and notes that 28 May is the highest-penalty day in the extract.
It constructs a same-day base-versus-submitted comparison for 29 May using the 12 pilot_revision blocks and fixed realized generation.

It tests relevant alternatives, including day-to-day baseline variability, selection and timing, the distinction between deviation metrics, and the possibility that lower DSM penalties do not imply higher net commercial value.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission calls 17.6% a 'modeled one-day estimate' and says the within-day association 'does not establish general causal efficacy'.
It explicitly identifies unknowns about outcome-informed selection, immutable timing, repeatability, and net value.
It specifies decision-changing evidence: pre-outcome records, matched pilot days, and reconciled penalty, meter, revenue, and pilot-cost data.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to hold expansion is proportionate to the one-day, non-randomized evidence.

The proposed next step—'Pre-register several matched high-wind days, preserve immutable pre-submission timestamps, and repeat the base-versus-submitted shadow calculation with net commercial value'—is discriminating and preserves operational safety.
It preserves the legitimate descriptive result by reporting 31.6% as the cross-day difference and 17.6% as the modeled one-day estimate.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion—'Credit the arithmetic, reject the attribution'—matches the supplied dynamics and the evidence limitations.
It retains a smaller same-day benefit rather than incorrectly concluding that the pilot had no value.
It accurately rejects both causal attribution of the full 31.6% and the stronger claim that the 17.6% estimate proves impact.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The phrase 'achieved a modeled penalty approximately Rs 549,664 versus Rs 453,086' could momentarily sound causal, although the submission immediately and appropriately qualifies it as a within-day association.
The statement that the shadow calculation is 'fully reversible' is an operational judgment rather than a claim directly established by the cited files.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent improvement may primarily reflect day-specific wind, forecast, dispatch, or selection conditions rather than the pilot. The 29 May base-versus-submitted comparison supports a modeled association, but without randomized or pre-registered matched comparisons it cannot separate pilot effect from the counterfactual's assumptions and block selection.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Validate the base_schedule_mw counterfactual and revision timing with immutable pre-submission records, then replicate the same-day shadow calculation across several pre-registered matched high-wind days while reconciling net commercial value.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Helios 90211090 is commercial ERP data."
"Declaration: P1001 declared with 90211000."
"commercial_invoice.pdf confirms P1001, 10 units, CHF 126,900 and air_waybill.pdf links SHP-000522 to CH-2025-000522. Neither proves legal classification."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Any differing string proves an error’: rejected because the Swiss reference lists 90211000 and warns Swiss/EU strings need not match."
"‘Helios master data supersedes local declaration filings’: rejected because Helios is commercial data without customs-ruling authority."
"The open question is Swiss legal code on 4 November 2025."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Swiss Matrix supports declared code but requires Tares confirmation."
"No record contradicts 90211000."
"Missing Evidence ... Swiss code on 2025-11-04 ... Effective Tares/ruling."
"Verification, not broker escalation, is proper."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Schema omits system/version/date/ruling authority."
"Helios in product_master_current.xlsx is commercial data, not ruling authority."
"Resolving schema deficiencies prevents repetitive false positives across Swiss entries."
"both share HS6 902110; local suffixes differ."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible mapping hold and request Tares or ruling confirmation."
"Escalate only if it contradicts 90211000; otherwise close the false positive and add jurisdiction/version/date to the comparator."
"This preserves both options while testing the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Swiss Matrix confirms 90211000 is valid for Switzerland" is somewhat stronger than the later qualification that it "requires Tares confirmation"; the matrix appears to support the code but not conclusively establish its legal validity on 4 November 2025.

"Binding classification requires official customs rulings" is stated as a general legal proposition without a cited authority and may overstate the role of rulings relative to effective tariff schedules or other official sources.
"Correct codes from different editions appear as mismatches without discrepancy" is a plausible general explanation but is not directly evidenced by the cited packet.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: 90211090 could reflect the legally applicable or more current classification, while 90211000 could be an outdated, incorrectly mapped, or otherwise nonbinding Swiss reference entry; the declaration should therefore remain unresolved until effective Tares data or an applicable ruling for 2025-11-04 is checked.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Cite the exact effective-date and jurisdiction fields or official Tares/ruling result, and distinguish clearly between a tariff-matrix reference, a legally effective classification, and commercial master data.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "IE-2025-000411 declares P1006 with Preference=Yes, United States origin, 0.0% duty, and 90211090." — `declaration.pdf`, IE-2025-000411, Line 1

"The airway bill links SHP-000411 to IE-2025-000411 but provides no `supplier_id`; the packet manifest lists six files and no shipment-specific supplier declaration." — `air_waybill.pdf`; `packet_manifest.txt`

"The reference lookup says no current document was found for SUP-02/P1006 and expressly says absence from the register does not prove that no document exists outside it." — `supplier_declaration_reference.txt`

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Preference=Yes proves the claim’: rejected because the indicator is a declaration field... while the packet lacks a linked supplier declaration"
"‘US ERP origin proves the claim is false’: rejected because `origin-workshop.md` explicitly says Helios is not a preference-proof system"
"The evidence reaches ‘not established,’ not ‘disproved.’"

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Unsupported is not the same as false. Verdict: unsupported, not disproved."
"The register explicitly notes that absence from the table does not prove no document exists outside it."
"The supplied extract shows 0.0% duty, so this hold is reversible and no duty change should be assumed until tariff treatment is confirmed."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "the workshop says manufacturing origin was never designed to prove preference."
"Resolving which supplier fulfilled this shipment and obtaining their valid declaration... is the required proof."
"The commercial invoice also states United States as P1006's manufacturing country"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "The correct disposition is a reversible hold, not an error or fraud referral."
"Hold the preference claim pending supplier-specific proof, request the declaration and governing rule from Procurement/Customs"
"do not clear it as preferential until verified."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "EU suppliers SUP-03/05/06 would allow linking active preference" is too broad: supplier location or a current register entry alone does not establish preferential origin; the applicable rule and shipment-specific supplier evidence are also required.
"SUP-01 would confirm non-preferential MFN" is not established merely by supplier identity or register status; the applicable tariff treatment and origin evidence must be verified.

"Valid declaration flips decision to clear as preferential" overstates the effect of a declaration unless it covers the shipment, identifies the relevant rule, and substantiates qualifying preferential origin.

"absence triggers administrative correction without fraud escalation" is a plausible safe process path but is not compelled by the cited evidence and should remain conditional on the compliance review.

"My inference is that this represents an evidence-tracking gap rather than commercial misrepresentation" is appropriately labeled an inference, but the available evidence cannot distinguish a tracking gap from other explanations.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06 may have supplied the shipment and a valid declaration may exist in procurement records outside the packet; consequently, the missing linkage supports an unverified claim, not a false claim. Conversely, the United States manufacturing-country field may reflect manufacturing rather than preferential origin and cannot resolve the claim either way.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the supplier-country alternatives conditional rather than treating EU supplier entries as sufficient, and specify that shipment linkage, the applicable preferential rule, and a valid supplier declaration must all be verified before clearing or correcting the claim.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The SOP defines the routine target from required evidence being available to disposition, but the extract has no timestamp for certificate/specification/deviation evidence availability."
"185 of 262 qcore_release_ts values are exactly 02:10:00, coinciding with the QCore daily snapshot time."
"For 220 completed rows, receipt-to-release mean is 45.5 hours, while lab-complete-to-release proxy mean/median are 26.9/21.3 hours."

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The SOP clock requires evidence_available_ts, which is missing from this extract."
"Using lab_complete_ts as an approximation introduces uncontrolled error because lab completion occurs both before and after receipt depending on testing protocols."
"True disposition time of 02:10 batches" is identified as a separate unknown to test.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "lab_complete_ts is only a proxy."
"missing/index-pending COA may be source lag rather than confirmed release without evidence."
"No—there is insufficient evidence because the required start timestamp is absent."

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Decision: Do not launch the ‘one and a half days’ KPI yet."
"Can this extract calculate the SOP's routine evidence-available-to-disposition KPI? No."
"Execute a targeted read-only spot-check of 5–10 batches in live QCore and CertVault."

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "‘The 1.5-day headline reflects genuine process speed’: rejected because 185 of 262 release timestamps ... are defaulted to 02:10:00 snapshot boundaries."
"‘Discard the extract as corrupt’: rejected because duration arithmetic is valid and monotonic."
"‘Immediate dashboard release is safe’: rejected because unmodeled evidence timestamps, right-censoring ... and snapshot defaults produce misleading management metrics."

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Live QCore timestamp audit capturing true certificate upload times"
"Read-only live audit of 10 batches with 02:10:00 extract timestamps"
"obtaining verified upload timestamps would resolve the true start of the release clock before building any report."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that 185 of 262 timestamps are defaulted and therefore 70.6% of release timestamps are synthetic may use all rows rather than only rows with release timestamps; the denominator and treatment of the 42 HOLD rows need reconciliation.

Calling the 02:10:00 values “synthetic snapshot artifacts” is stronger than the direct observation that they are concentrated at the QCore snapshot time; an interface-commit timestamp or extraction-boundary explanation remains open.

The phrase “evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours” is not adequately defined and appears inconsistent with the admission that evidence_available_ts is absent; it should be labeled as a proxy and its start field specified.
The submission references source freshness but does not explicitly establish that QCore and LabTrack extracts are not a coherent point-in-time snapshot before combining them.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The process may genuinely have material workflow delay, especially in lab completion or queue handling, while the 02:10 concentration adds a separate measurement artifact. The current extract cannot determine the relative contribution of workflow time versus interface/extraction timing.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain a minimally scoped event-level extract or audit for a sampled set of batches containing required-evidence availability, true disposition/decision time, interface commit time, source system, and extraction timestamps; reconcile the denominator and 02:10 rows, then recompute the KPI with open HOLD rows treated as right-censored.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “An exact join on manufacturer part numbers across `part_requests.csv` and `spare_parts.csv` retrieves every identified request.” — Specific files, fields, and request IDs are identified; however, the submission rarely gives row-level values or direct quotations for the supporting records.
“The global stock snapshot is dated 26 June while the request export is associated with the 24 July ProcureNet snapshot.” — Freshness and counterevidence are explicitly linked to the decision.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: “Every search hit represents a direct transfer opportunity”: rejected. PR-260700/704/712/715 match MTR-4401, yet ... [stock is] reserved ... or zero.” — Separates candidate retrieval from transfer eligibility and tests a competing explanation.

“Same part family means interchangeable”: rejected. PR-260705 and PR-260720 require ... revision A, while stocked units are revision B.” — Uses revision as a causal decision constraint rather than treating description similarity as equivalence.

The reasoning is strong on identity, revision, reservation, quantity, and qualification, but the claim that semantic search is not the real problem is based on a small 24-request sample and remains somewhat under-tested.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “Treat search results as candidates, not automatic transfers.” — Appropriately limits the operational interpretation of search output.
“Actionable now still requires current confirmation.” — Downgrades certainty because the global stock snapshot is older than the request export.

“Needs check” and “Not transferable on current evidence” — Uses claim-specific classifications, although “Actionable now” is somewhat stronger than warranted given the acknowledged stale global snapshot.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: “Defend only the eight-request actionable slice, not gross value.” — Reframes the decision from gross theoretical savings to safeguarded actionable value.
“Test data hygiene and exact matching first.” — Proposes a lower-cost, reversible priority before investing in an expensive semantic-search system.
“Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search on 24 requests.” — Defines a practical pilot and a decision criterion while preserving engineering and availability confirmation.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: “Every search hit represents a direct transfer opportunity”: rejected ... reserved ... or zero stock.”
“Same part family means interchangeable”: rejected ... revision A ... revision B.”
“available_qty_global=-1 means zero stock”: rejected ... -1 is a verification sentinel indicating reservation lag.”
“The hypothesis survives only if records are wrong, requiring a live CMMS check.” — Addresses the strongest alternative explanations and states what evidence could revive the rejected interpretation.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: “Manufacturer part number and revision from local maintenance records” and “Live local CMMS reservation and availability query” — Requests targeted evidence tied directly to the decision bottlenecks.
“Receiving engineer and qualification approval” — Identifies the specific decision owner for revision and site-specific substitution.
“Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search on 24 requests” — Requests a bounded test with explicit expected decision impact rather than generic additional data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Semantic search is not the real problem” is too broad from a 24-request sample: exact MPN matching covers the 13 identified requests, but the 11 blank-MPN requests are precisely where semantic retrieval may add value.
The label “Actionable now” is slightly overstated while the submission simultaneously acknowledges that the global stock snapshot is stale and current CMMS confirmation is still required.

“All four not-transferable requests” is well supported as a current-evidence classification, but should not be read as a permanent impossibility because live reservation and stock records could change.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Exact MPN matching may be sufficient for the identified subset but not for the 11 blank-MPN requests; semantic search could materially improve candidate recall there, with the apparent data-hygiene problem and search-value question requiring a blinded comparison against maintenance-record identities and engineer validation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run the proposed 24-request exact-versus-semantic comparison, especially on the 11 blank-MPN requests, using manufacturer identity, revision, UOM, qualification, and live availability as validation labels; report candidate value separately from confirmed transferable value.
